title: The Reality of Resurrection and the Defeat of Death
english: the passion

Were the events concerning Lazarus not a phantom? Were the events concerning the daughter of Jairus not a dream? Were the events concerning the widow's son not a shadow? But the things that happened were truth. How then can he who has despoiled death fear death? How can he who raises the dead with authority pray and be cowardly toward death, fearing to fall? For even if you fall, he will set you free. For he who raises others much more raises his own body.

Therefore, explain the meaning to me, Lord, or cease this speech and do not exhaust my soul, or make my reasoning stumble. For if you are the one who knew all things before their coming into being, how do you now be ignorant whether it is possible or impossible for the cup to pass? For if you are ignorant, Paul lies, saying that there is no creation hidden from your sight, but all things are naked and laid bare to his eyes (Hebrews 4:13). But if you know, why do you say, 'Is it possible?' For when one is ignorant, it is a question, and when one is not knowing, it is a decision. Therefore, explain to us, Lord, the meaning of the things said. For now Eunomius rejoices, now Arius is delighted, snatching the word for the hypothesis of blasphemy. But they rejoice in vain. For it is not for the ungodly to rejoice, says the Lord (Psalm 2:4). I do not fear death, as they say; I do not decline the passion, as they think.

For if he did not wish to grant life through death to the race of humans, being a passionless Word, he would not have entered into suffering flesh. Since he saw the race of humans held by deception and not by necessity, by the seduction of demons and not by force, he descended into your body, so that having constructed the opposites from the opposites through every deception, he might set the human free. Because the tyrant thought greatly that, finding sin and bringing death through sin, he had made the citizen of Paradise, Adam—the appointed master of the inhabited world—a slave, a robber, and a thief; because of this, he set the earth apart as a king, having the flesh as a stronghold, so that, by decapitating the tyrant's insolence, he might undo the deception with deception, muster righteousness against sin, and touch life through death. Therefore, not fearing death, I am not cowardly; for the matter is not unintentional, but the deed is self-chosen. For I am the good shepherd who...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Master of Nature and the Incarnation
english: He voluntarily offers his own soul for the sheep. Just as, existing in the form of God, he emptied himself by taking the form of a slave, not compelled by any necessity, so also he willingly undergoes death, not held by force, but coming to the passion of his own accord.

For what did he suffer, Master? For the salvation of mankind, he says. And I state the manner. Because the race of men was subjected to the decree of death through Adam, who was formed from a virgin earth, and I am the one casting out the decree of death, it was impossible for the punishment to be lifted from man unless I myself recalled my own decree; therefore, having taken the form of a man in likeness to Adam from a virgin womb, I undergo death, so that as God I might loose the decree and as man I might receive death on behalf of men.

I do this so that I might free man not by authority, but by sympathy. For if God had been the one who succeeded through a man sinning, the succeeding would not have been great. But now, because of this, I have become man, and for the sake of the one who abolished the law, I fulfilled the law, so that the race of men might spring forth from the intimacy of the one who succeeded.

Therefore also now, in the person of Adam, I receive the decree of death, so that he might receive through me the grace of the resurrection. Adam, having sinned, brought in death; I, having succeeded, brought in the resurrection. And because death reigned from Adam until Moses, and reigned because the body holds the accomplice of sin at hand, therefore I took up that same body which seems to be the instrument of sin, so that, having abolished sin, I might prove man free from sin.

Otherwise, because men were living an evil life, entangled in sin, since their life was more akin to death, therefore I choose the good death over the evil life and undergo death, so that those participating in the good death might enjoy the true life; and they enjoy it through baptism. For as many as are baptized are baptized into my death, so that just as I was raised from the dead, so also they might walk in a newness of life. And let no one wavering say that darkness does not work light, nor blackness produce whiteness, how then death...

How [is it] the life? For the matter is clearly beyond nature. But do not seek a natural order in me. For I am the master of nature, who at times allows nature to act according to its nature, and at times guides it beyond nature. For when I wish to manage something wondrously, then even nature, having denied its own order, does that which my guiding spirit directs.

And this is clear from the observed arrangement; I say something like this: the sun and the moon are fire according to nature, but the crystallized solid, which I called heaven, is water. If therefore you seek a natural course, how is the fire kept by the water, or how is the crystallized solid not dissolved and flowed away by the heat of the fire? And so that I may not occupy your soul regarding the observed arrangement, I persuade you, having manipulated the economy through it, that it is not right to seek a course in the paradoxical wonders of nature.

For calculate that, being God, I condescended to a human body. This indeed is first against nature. For tell me, how could the human body, which is divided by a hair, contain the uncontainable, the immeasurable, the one being everywhere, the one encompassing the whole inhabited world, the one measuring the heaven with a spark, the earth with a dragon, and the sea with a cup? For that he contained is clear, since even the full essence of deity dwelt in the flesh bodily (Colossians 2:9). But as for 'how', he says. For I know what I manage, but you are not able to hear; for the knowledge of the secret things surpasses mortal hearing, such that even if at times I wish to interpret something through a multitude of mercies, I interpret it not as nature is, but as you are able to learn; for this reason also, suppressing the blindness of those who will seem wise, I was saying: He who thinks he knows something, has not yet known anything, as it is necessary to know.

Since you have heard that being the Word I have become flesh (John 1:14), but you are ignorant of the 'how'. For how was I in the flesh, as a body in a body or as a soul in a body? Surely I suffered with the suffering body, but I did not suffer. For the nature of God does not fall into passion. Just as I have become flesh without ceasing to be God, so also I underwent passion without falling into passion. I was born through economy, I died for the salvation of men; rather, I died because of this, because I was born. Do not therefore seek in me either the order of birth or...

title: The Fisherman's Bait
english: In the manner of death. For nature does not do these things, but power accomplishes them. Being God, therefore, I descended into a human body. This was first contrary to nature; but it did not happen through nature as an impossibility, because it lay within my authority, the one who created nature.

I also consented again for the body itself to fall into general death, so that life, mastering death, might demonstrate its energy within that death. The living living is not wonderful, but the dead living is this great and paradoxical thing. Therefore I also consented to be dissolved, and after being dissolved I rose, so that I might show that even after the body was subjected to death, I remained thus impassive, because I raised not only my own body, but also the bodies of the sleeping righteous together with me.

Voluntarily, therefore, through philanthropy I undergo death, but voluntarily, according to some economy, I feign cowardice. For I feign cowardice so that I might deceive death. Just as in the desert, if I had not become hungry, the devil would not have approached (Matt 4:3). But because of this I became hungry, so that, not thinking there was another Adam, he might bring the beast. Thus also here, because of this, I offer the word of cowardice as bait, so that I might hook death for myself.

For when the devil saw many signs having been performed: paralyzing nerves, joining tongues that were wandering, opening deaf ears, giving sight to the blind, turning the surge of the sea into calm, drying up the bleeding springs by the touch of the vessel, raising Lazarus by the word (John 11:43), raising the daughter of Jairus (Mark 5:41), calling up the son of the widow from the dead (Luke 7:14); all these things having seen and having been persuaded by these deeds, that I am the Son of God having appeared in the form of man according to the prophecy of the prophets, he fears and is terrified to crucify me and hand me over to death, lest, having entered under the form of a dead man, I might free the dead.

What then do I do, so that I might also transform the cowardice of the devil into madness and make him attack death? I flee so that he may pursue, I feign cowardice so that he may be emboldened; I use lowly words so that, thinking me one of many, he may rush upon and overwhelm me. For if he does not overwhelm me, he will not be able to overwhelm those who are laid upon me. Therefore I speak words of cowardice, in order to—

Having deceived the deceiver, I will undo the deception. That one deceived Adam with deceitful words; I deceive the deceiver with cowardly words. But he spoke words to deceivers in order to destroy man, while I speak words of cowardice in order to free the inhabited world.

I am a fisherman fishing. For just as a fisherman, having placed a worm on a hook, extends the rod and sometimes gives the hook and sometimes pulls and withdraws, so that by showing the fleeing worm he might prepare to strike the fish, so also I, having placed the body like a worm on the hook of my divinity—for I am a worm and not a man—sometimes pull death as a coward, and sometimes give the hook as a brave man, so that the devil, as a fish falling upon the worm, that is, coming upon the flesh, might secretly fall upon the hook of divinity and, having fallen, be pulled, so that what was said by Job might be fulfilled upon him: 'You shall draw a dragon with a hook' (Job 41:1).

Therefore, not fearing death, I said: 'My soul is in great distress' (Psalm 91:7). Nor do I say I am cowardly to suffer: 'Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me' (Matthew 26:39). For I do all things so that death might not escape me. I act cowardly as a man, so that having laid it down as a man, I may work as God.

I have used lowly words, so that by consuming my leaven of the flesh, he might find the coal of divinity fiercely burning him. I act cowardly so that my body might chew a grain of mustard seed, and he will find the sharpness of divinity severely tormenting him. I act cowardly so that he might swallow me as a man. For if he swallows me, he will find the hard rock of divinity crushing his teeth, so that what is written might be fulfilled upon him: 'God will crush his teeth in his mouth' (Psalm 3:7).

Therefore, I hide the authority of the divinity and put forward the cowardice of the flesh, so that he might not be hunted by the power of divinity, but might be cast down by the weakness of the body. For lest he think highly of himself as being defeated by God, for this reason I deceive him through the flesh, so that he might be attacked through those things by which he planned to attack. I therefore conquer him through the weakness of the body, so that he might not think highly of himself as being rebuked by divine power. For that which is by the divinity...
